fact: The World Bank ISR says a clean payroll database is being used to pay civil servants and civil-servant enrolment on the government salary mobile payment system (Patapaye) increased.

The Patapaye project, funded by the World Bank, IMF and EU, began a mobile money salary-payment test in March 2020 with about 250 employees, and authorities announced enrolment of civil servants intensified across at least 14 prefectures.

Business & Finance International reports that civil servants' salaries are domiciled at Ecobank Centrafrique and the Banque populaire maroco-centrafricaine, and that bank transfers exist alongside direct cash payment as salary payment modes.

RFI reports that public administrations in the Central African Republic transfer employees' monthly salaries into bank accounts between the 20th and 30th of each month, though provincial civil servants must travel to Bangui to collect them.

The World Bank G2Px blog reports that public wage recipients in the Central African Republic expressed high satisfaction with mobile money salary payments, having before 2020 travelled up to two days to collect cash salaries.
